documents.title: Primary Care Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Diabetes / BP f/u. Missed the December slot (snowed in), rebooked today.
Using the pill box every day since the fall, no more confusion about the lisinopril. Drinking about the same, he says maybe a few fewer on weekdays. No hypoglycemia symptoms, no foot problems.
Exam: pleasant, NAD. RRR, lungs clear, no edema. Feet: intact skin, sensation intact.
A1c 7.2 today; BMP otherwise normal.
A/P: T2DM stable on metformin. HTN controlled since the label fix. Med adherence: working with the organizer, keep it on the problem list for now. AUD: counseled, declines treatment. Shingrix #2 today, series complete. Wellness visit in June with fasting labs.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Medicare AWV.
Health risk assessment reviewed with him. Independent in all ADLs and IADLs, drives, at home in Chesterfield. No falls this year. Hearing and vision adequate by his report. Mood fine; PHQ-2 negative. AUDIT-C 12. Uses a seatbelt; smoke detectors in the house.
Advance directive: none; he wants to think about who would be his health care proxy. Form given.

Meds reviewed bottle by bottle: metformin 1000 BID, lisinopril 10 daily, atorvastatin 40 daily. All in the organizer.

Exam: BP and weight in flowsheet. Alert, oriented. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, liver not enlarged. Skin unremarkable. Feet: monofilament intact, pulses palpable. Gait steady.

Screening: colonoscopy 2017 normal, next 2027. Hep C and HIV done 2020. Pneumococcal series complete. Shingrix complete. Flu and COVID in the fall.

Alcohol: still 6 to 8 a day. Asked again about naltrexone, explained it can blunt the urge and is taken once a day; he says not yet. Offered a counseling referral, also not yet.

Plan: fasting labs drawn. Eye exam with his optometrist this summer, send the report. Return in about 5 months for diabetes.

documents.title: Results From Your Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Francis, your bloodwork looks steady. A1c 6.9. Liver and kidney numbers normal, blood counts normal, urine protein normal. Cholesterol about where it was. Same medicines, same doses.

documents.title: Diabetic Eye Examination
documents.author: optometry
documents.body:
Dilated eye examination, performed 07/19/2022.
Patient: Francis Sawyer. History: type 2 diabetes.
Corrected visual acuity good each eye. Pupils equal and reactive. Anterior segment normal. Dilated fundus: clear media, healthy optic nerves, no hemorrhages, exudates or neovascularization either eye.
Impression: no diabetic retinopathy.
Recommend repeat in 12 months.
Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Nurse Visit: Immunizations
documents.author: RN
documents.body: High-dose flu L arm and bivalent COVID R arm. Feels well, afebrile. Observed 15 minutes, fine. Reminded him of his diabetes visit next month.

orders.reason: Progressive right hand stiffness, cannot straighten fingers

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Primary Care Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Diabetes check, plus a new complaint.
Right hand: for a few years has been getting stiffer, and now some fingers will not straighten all the way. Hard to grip a hammer or get his hand into a glove. No injury he remembers. No pain to speak of, no numbness.
Otherwise steady. Taking his meds from the organizer. Drinking unchanged.

Exam: vitals in flowsheet. Heart and lungs normal. Right hand: firm thickening across the palm, fingers lack full extension. Grip reasonable. Sensation intact in all fingertips, radial pulse normal.

A1c 7.2.

A/P
1. Right hand: looks like a palmar fascia problem rather than a tendon or nerve issue. Orthopedics referral placed.
2. T2DM: A1c 7.2, continue metformin.
3. HTN, HLD: continue.
4. AUD: counseled briefly.
RTC 4 months.

documents.title: Records Request: Orthopedics
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pt called to update a phone number on file and mentioned he saw the orthopedic doctor right before Christmas. He says they told him what it was and to keep an eye on it. No consult letter here yet. Request faxed to the orthopedic office.

documents.title: Orthopedics Consultation
documents.author: orthopedics
documents.body:
Outside orthopedics consultation. Date of service: 12/23/2022. Sent on request.

Reason for referral: right hand stiffness.

HPI: 68-year-old man, retired from construction, referred by his primary physician. He was seen there for diabetes care and for a period of mixed-up blood pressure dosing. Over several years the right hand has grown steadily stiffer and some fingers no longer straighten, so gripping tools and everyday jobs have become harder. Describes the hand as tight. Once a finger curls down it stays down; no catching or popping, and the stiffness does not come and go. No injury, redness or acute pain. No numbness or tingling.

PMH: type 2 diabetes, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, long-standing heavy alcohol use.
Medications: metformin 1000 mg twice daily, lisinopril 10 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Social: retired, mostly at home. Never smoker.
Family: father diabetes, mother hypertension, paternal grandfather MI at 72.

Exam, right hand: palpable longitudinal cords in the palm; fingers cannot be brought fully straight. No triggering. No skin breakdown. Sensation intact to light touch in all digits. Radial pulse palpable, capillary refill brisk.

Assessment: Dupuytren contracture, right hand.

Plan: discussed the nature of the condition, that it tends to progress slowly and is linked with diabetes and alcohol. No intervention now. He can check at home by trying to lay the hand flat on a table; if it no longer lies flat or function worsens, referral to hand surgery for treatment options. Follow up as needed.

Copy to primary care physician.

documents.title: Outside Letter Reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Ortho letter reviewed. Dupuytren contracture of the right hand, observation for now. Added to problem list. Will check the tabletop test at visits.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Primary Care Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
F/u T2DM, HTN.
Ortho told him the same as their letter: Dupuytren's, watch it. Right hand about the same as November. Can still get the palm nearly flat on the desk here.
Taking meds daily. A few more drinks over the winter than he'd like.
Exam: vitals OK. Heart, lungs normal. R palm cords as before. Feet fine.
A1c 7.1, BMP otherwise normal.
A/P: T2DM A1c 7.1, about the same; no med change, recheck at AWV. HTN controlled. Dupuytren R hand, observe. AUD: counseled again. RTC June for AWV.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Subsequent AWV.
HRA reviewed: independent, no falls, drives. PHQ-2 negative. AUDIT-C 11, slightly down; says he has stopped drinking before noon. Never smoker.
Health care proxy form: still not filled out; he is still deciding whom to name.
Meds: metformin 1000 BID, lisinopril 10, atorvastatin 40. Organizer in use.
Exam: flowsheet vitals. Alert. Heart regular without murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, no liver edge. Right palm cords unchanged. Feet: sensation and pulses normal.
Prevention: colonoscopy due 2027. Vaccines up to date except fall flu/COVID.
Alcohol: acknowledged the small step; naltrexone offered again, declined.
Plan: labs today. Optometry exam due, he has not booked it yet; reminded. Diabetes visit in September.

documents.title: Nurse Visit: Immunizations
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu (high dose) and 2023-24 COVID given. He apologized for missing his September appointment, forgot it was a Monday. Rebooked with PCP for 10/23. No reaction after 15 min.

documents.title: Primary Care Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Rescheduled diabetes visit.
Feels fine. Organizer in use. Still drinking most evenings. Never got to the eye doctor this summer; says he will call them.
R hand: no real change; can just about flatten it on the table.
Exam: vitals fine. Heart, lungs clear. No edema.
A1c 7.1.
A/P: T2DM controlled, metformin unchanged. HTN controlled. HLD on atorvastatin. Dupuytren R, observe. AUD counseled. Eye exam reminder. RTC 4 to 5 months.
